newsitem.title: USA: Merger activity stirs quiet US corporate bond mart.
newsitem.headline: Merger activity stirs quiet US corporate bond mart.

text.p: Entergy Corp's bid for London Electricity and Avenor Inc's offer to buy out Repap Enterprises Inc, generated significant trading activity in an otherwise sleepy U.S. corporate bond market on Wednesday, traders said.
Spreads on senior debt of two Entergy subsidiaries, Entergy Gulf States Inc and Systems Energy Resources Inc, widened around 20 basis points on news of the potential merger, traders said.
Traders say the units' bonds are at risk of being downgraded to split-rated status if the aquisition occurs.

Standard & Poor's announced on Wednesday that it will consider cutting the debt ratings of all Entergy subsidiaries and London Electricity. Moody's Investors Service said it was only considering downgrading the debt of London Electricity, but not any of Entergy's six operating subsidiaries.

"S&P is more negative about the fundamentals of the utility industry. Against that backdrop, to come out with a highly leveraged purchase, jeopordizes the ratings of Entergy's weaker subs," said Dan Scotto, head of investment grade corporate bond research at Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
